title: What each Jacobian column means physically

items.stem: For a serial arm, column i of the Jacobian maps joint rates to the motion of the end-effector reference point (the endpoint). Which description of column i is correct?

options.text: The partial derivative of the endpoint's roll-pitch-yaw angles with respect to the joint angle θᵢ, with all other joints held still
The endpoint's velocity when every joint moves at unit rate together, with one such column for each joint
The endpoint's linear and angular velocity when only joint i moves at unit rate and the others are held still
The velocity of the origin of frame i when joint i alone moves at unit rate and the others are held still

items.stem: A planar arm has two rotary joints with parallel vertical axes. Link 1 is 0.4 m long and link 2 is 0.3 m long, and the arm is stretched out straight. The endpoint is the tip of link 2. Only joint 1 turns, at 2 rad/s, and joint 2 is held still. What is the speed of the endpoint, in m/s?

An arm has joint 1 rotating about the vertical base z-axis, and joint 2 rotating about a horizontal axis. When θ₁ = 0°, joint 2's axis points along the base +y direction. The arm is now posed with θ₁ = 90° (a counterclockwise turn about +z, seen from above). What is the base-frame x-component of the angular part of Jacobian column 2, in rad/s per rad/s? Use the right-hand rule for the direction of the axis.
A prismatic (sliding) joint has an axis direction given by the unit vector z in the base frame. Which pair gives the linear part and the angular part of that joint's Jacobian column?

options.text: Linear part: the axis z itself. Angular part: zero.
Linear part: z crossed with the vector from the joint to the endpoint. Angular part: z.
Linear part: zero. Angular part: the axis z itself.
Linear part: z crossed with the vector from the joint to the endpoint. Angular part: zero.

items.stem: In a planar arm with two rotary joints with parallel vertical axes (link 1 is 0.4 m, link 2 is 0.3 m, endpoint at the tip of link 2), what is the angular part of Jacobian column 2 in base coordinates? Use a 6-row Jacobian with the linear rows on top and the angular rows (the bottom three entries) below.

options.text: (0, 0, 0), because the endpoint's orientation does not change with joint 2
(0, 0, 0.3), because it scales with the length of link 2
(0, 0, 0.7), because it scales with the distance from the base to the endpoint
(0, 0, 1), because the endpoint turns about the vertical axis at the joint's rate

items.stem: An arm has rotary and prismatic joints. The Jacobian is first written for the wrist as the endpoint, and then rewritten for a tool tip fixed rigidly 0.2 m beyond the wrist, off all the rotary axes. Which entries of the matrix change?

options.text: The linear and angular parts of every column
Only the linear parts of the rotary-joint columns
The linear parts of every column, rotary and prismatic
The linear parts of the rotary columns and the angular parts of the prismatic columns
